name: har_oneshot_v1
status: DRAFT 2 for the research-reviewer. Nothing in it has been run, and its author has loaded, read, computed on or printed no price, return, variance or loss of any session on or after 2023-03-01 (the committed documents quoted below, written by the data steward, are the only window information it relies on, and the disclosure section says what they showed). It binds only once merged; the evaluation may not be run before the merge, and the sha256 of the merged file is recorded with the run.
relation: the one-shot out-of-sample evaluation that docs/ML_PHASE0.md (tier T1b) and docs/ML_RESEARCH_PLAN.md (M1) promised for the locked HAR model of vol_forecast_v1 (spec sha256 f2d4d047ee19a607b539eda60d187f1b35ad02f1e42f6025a0cfa6b79b74e637). That spec's own lock (2019-01-01 to 2023-02-28) is spent and is not reopened or re-tested for a decision; this spec reads from it its candidates, its loss, its test, its committed lock scores (only as the control below) and its committed dev-period numbers (the power paragraph).
dataset: the owner's Kaggle source debashis74017/nifty-50-minute-data (version 18), imported by P0.2 as dataset ml-intake-2-feae259bdba6, digest 47d28d6376ca63af (docs/EXTERNAL_DATA.md), tier T1b; use: regime_research. The evaluation reads this digest and no other. It is run only when the dataset is external_verified, that is, only when a verification.json written by the P0.6 check names this digest and says it passed (see run_only_after_p06). The aeron7 import ends in Feb 2023 and cannot supply the window, so every Kaggle session the run touches, before and inside the window, comes from this one table.

run_only_after_p06.rule: the evaluation is RUN ONLY AFTER P0.6 (the independent check of the 2023 to 2026 index minutes, docs/ML_PHASE0.md) has checked the Mar 2023 to May 2026 stretch of this digest and passed it. Nothing is urgent, and without this a source defect in that stretch would be scored as model error. The command has no flag that accepts an unverified dataset: it refuses a dataset that is not external_verified for the digest named here
run_only_after_p06.if_p06_rejects_or_changes_the_data: the dataset is not used: no look is spent, because the look is spent only when the run happens. A different digest (an importer fix, an admitted review session, a patched stretch) is a different dataset and needs a new spec; this one is never edited
run_only_after_p06.what_p06_may_see: P0.6 compares prices with other sources; it computes no forecast, no loss and no realised-variance ranking of the window, and its report is committed before the run. The data steward has already seen the window's variance ranks (disclosure below); P0.6 adds nothing of that kind
run_only_after_p06.label: the result says 'evidence: external_verified (underlying only)' only if the verification record is present when it runs, and says so with the record's own hash. The tier stays T1b and the use stays research: it cannot support a live change, a promotion, a paper-gate step, an option-strategy claim or a profitability claim, verified or not

not_for: no option prices: nothing here qualifies an option strategy, a DTE change, a paper gate, a promotion, a live change or a profitability claim
question: does the locked, deployed HAR model (C_har as stored in quantdesk/intraday/vol_har_v1.json, never refitted) forecast the realised variance of the next 30m / 60m / 120m / to the close better than the desk's VolForecaster (A_desk) on 1 Mar 2023 to 14 May 2026, which nobody has scored

window.note: the reserved window of quantdesk/ml/build.py (RESERVED_FROM) to the last session the dataset keeps: the importer rejects 15 May 2026 as truncated (docs/EXTERNAL_DATA.md, items 5 and 14), so the window effectively ends on 14 May 2026. 15 May to early Sep 2026 is a hole in the data; later sessions (the desk's own tape, a filled hole) need a new spec

decision_points: every 15 minutes from 09:30 to 15:00 IST (volstudy.DECISIONS), exactly as vol_forecast_v1
target: realised variance over (t, t+h]: the sum of squared 1-minute log returns, close to close (no range-based input, the two sources differ on highs and lows); for 'close' to the 15:29 bar (volstudy.rows, unchanged); horizons 30m, 60m, 120m, close. A missing minute inside a kept session is forward-filled by volstudy.grid and a label window with more than 20% of its minutes missing is dropped (miss_frac), as in the locked study

frozen_model.which: C_har, the candidate vol_forecast_v1 selected on dev for all four horizons and that passed its lock in all 8 cells (docs/prereg/results/vol_forecast_v1-f2d4d047ee19.md), in the form the desk deploys it
frozen_model.strict_reuse: PRIMARY. The coefficients and the minute-of-day profile are those committed in quantdesk/intraday/vol_har_v1.json (sha256 de59c4ab9496e9ae2bc828741686949bf5608a2c4af548ce064afa25b3bef56a, the pin in quantdesk/intraday/volshadow.py COEF_PIN): fitted offline by autolearn vol-har-fit on the aeron7 import (dataset aeron7-2-906fc2378b, external_verified) over every accepted session from 2010-01-04 to 2018-12-31 (NIFTY 2013 sessions, BANKNIFTY 2009), the spec's own training window, and not refitted since ('the desk never refits'). The run refuses a file whose sha256 differs from that pin. Nothing is fitted on the Kaggle data or on the window for the primary test
frozen_model.profile: A_desk has no profile. B_seasonal and C_har use the artifact's profile for each symbol (375 values), the same one the locked lock test used, not a profile fitted on the Kaggle data. build_tables will need a small `profile=` argument ({symbol: the 375 values}) that replaces fit_profile for the symbol, bypasses MIN_PROFILE_DAYS and puts the profile's sha256 into the recipe and so the table's identity; it is described here and not implemented. Rows are still marked in_profile with profile_end '2018-12-31' (the artifact's dev_end, the last session its profile and coefficients saw), so no scored row is in the profile window
frozen_model.frozen: no coefficient, smearing factor, profile, hyper-parameter, feature, horizon or candidate is chosen, refitted or re-selected on the window. They are copied unchanged into the result file with the artifact's sha256
frozen_model.refit_secondary: REGISTERED, NON-DECISIVE (staleness vs structure). The same C_har structure and A/B definitions refitted once on the Kaggle table: profile_end 2023-02-28 (the day before RESERVED_FROM; build_tables accepts it without allow_reserved_profile), training on every Kaggle session from 2015-01-09 to 2023-02-28, then frozen. It is scored on the same window rows beside the primary and never enters the pass/fail or kill logic. Its training rows are obtained from a second table (profile_end 2023-02-28, its own identity) read with build.load_table(scoring_only=False, reserved_spec=<this file>) and split by in_profile: in_profile True rows (all dated 2023-02-28 or earlier) train, in_profile False rows (the reserved window) are scored, with splits.check_test_mask asserting that no scored row is in the training set. The default load_table path, scoring_only=True, withholds the in_profile rows and so cannot be used for this fit. It answers whether any shortfall of the primary is staleness of the 2018 coefficients (the refit recovers it) or structure (it does not)

candidates.A_desk: the desk's VolForecaster without IV: EWMA (half-life 30 min) of today's 1-minute squared returns blended with the prior 5 sessions' mean with weight n/(n+60); horizon variance = per-minute variance x minutes. Nothing is fitted
candidates.B_seasonal: A computed on returns divided by the minute-of-day profile (the artifact's); horizon variance = deseasonalised per-minute variance x the sum of the profile over the horizon's minutes
candidates.C_har: the frozen model above (the deployed artifact)

baselines: A_desk is the baseline of the primary test (it is what the desk runs). B_seasonal, the other candidate already in the study and the one that needs no fit, is the baseline of the pooled C-versus-B test and of the secondary comparisons. No new candidate, no other baseline, no model added after registration
loss: QLIKE = RV/F - log(RV/F) - 1 (volstudy.qlike, floor 1e-12), averaged per day over that day's decision points and horizon rows, then over days (volstudy.daily_loss / score), unchanged

primary_test.statement: for each symbol and each horizon, H0: the frozen C_har's mean daily QLIKE is not lower than A_desk's; H1: it is lower
primary_test.statistic: d_t = daily QLIKE of A_desk minus daily QLIKE of C_har on session t of the window; Diebold-Mariano t = nw_t(d) with Newey-West, 5 lags (autolearn.prereg.nw_t, Bartlett weights, the rule of vol_forecast_v1); one-sided p = 1 - Phi(t) (normal), as the locked study. nw_t returns NaN for fewer than 10 sessions or a non-positive variance: such a cell has no p-value and does not pass
primary_test.cells: NIFTY x {30m, 60m, 120m, close} and BANKNIFTY x {30m, 60m, 120m, close}: 8 cells
primary_test.family: these 8 cells are the whole family that decides PASS and KILL; no other p-value decides either
primary_test.correction: Holm-Bonferroni across the 8 one-sided p-values, familywise error 0.05 (valid under any dependence, which matters because the two indices and the four horizons are strongly correlated). A cell passes when its Holm-adjusted p is below 0.05; a NaN or undersized cell is counted as not passing and is ranked last in Holm's ordering. This is stricter than vol_forecast_v1, which tested each cell at an uncorrected 0.05; the change is deliberate, because the family here is the whole claim

pooled_cb_test.purpose: the one pre-declared question of whether the HAR layer adds anything beyond the seasonal profile. It sits OUTSIDE the PASS/KILL family and gates only the sentence 'the HAR layer adds beyond the seasonal profile'
pooled_cb_test.statistic: e_t = for each session date t, the mean over the cells present that day (up to the 8: 2 symbols x 4 horizons) of the cell's daily QLIKE of B_seasonal minus that of the frozen C_har; one Diebold-Mariano t = nw_t(e) with Newey-West, 5 lags, one-sided p = 1 - Phi(t), significance level 0.05, no correction (a single test)
pooled_cb_test.consequence: if p < 0.05 the result may say that the HAR layer adds beyond the seasonal profile on this window; if not (or NaN), it must say that B_seasonal, which needs no fit, is the cheaper alternative, and it may not say that the HAR layer adds

secondary_descriptive: reported, never decisive, outside the family and uncorrected: the refit of the same structure on the Kaggle table (frozen_model.refit_secondary) against A_desk, B_seasonal and the frozen C_har, per cell; the per-cell Diebold-Mariano of the frozen C_har against B_seasonal; B against A; QLIKE, log-forecast-error bias and the move ratio by time-of-day bucket (volstudy.score) per candidate; the cells split by calendar year of the window; the Newey-West t at 10 and 20 lags; the daily loss differences' autocorrelations. A secondary result that disagrees with the primary one does not change the verdict; it is stated beside it

pass_fail.PASS: all 8 cells pass (Holm-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05 for the frozen C_har against A_desk) and in each cell C_har's mean daily QLIKE is lower than A_desk's
pass_fail.MIXED: one to three cells do not pass (including a NaN or undersized cell) and none of the 8 has a mean QLIKE for C_har at or above A_desk's. Reported cell by cell; the model is neither confirmed nor retired
pass_fail.KILL: four or more cells do not pass (a NaN or undersized cell counts as not passing), or any single cell has C_har's mean daily QLIKE at or above A_desk's. The second condition is a registered hair-trigger: one cell, on one index and one horizon, retires the model whatever the other seven show, and it is accepted in advance as the price of a rule that cannot be argued around after the outcome
pass_fail.FAIL: MIXED or KILL: anything that is not PASS
pass_fail.meaning_of_pass: the deployed HAR model, with coefficients fixed in 2018 and never refitted, beat the desk's present forecaster out of sample on this window and in every index and horizon. It does not say the HAR layer improves on the seasonal profile: that is the pooled C-versus-B test, and unless it passes the result states that B_seasonal, which needs no fit, is the cheaper alternative. It does not touch option plans. Its only consequence is that the model may be carried forward as an offline research candidate for M1 and for the desk's realised-volatility input, pending a separate reviewed change

kill_rule: on KILL the locked HAR model is retired as a candidate to replace the desk's realised-variance input: it is not re-tuned, re-fitted or re-selected on this window (the refit secondary is descriptive and does not rescue it), the window is not used to look for a better model, and any successor needs a new spec and data nobody has scored (the desk's own tape from Oct 2026 on, T2). A MIXED or KILL outcome is written up as such, with every cell, in the same file as a PASS would be. The result is not softened by a secondary analysis, a different correction, a subset of years or a re-run. Because the evaluation is run only after P0.6 has passed the data, a KILL is final: it cannot later be blamed on, or voided by, a source defect

looks.rule: exactly one evaluation of the window. The look is spent only when the run happens, that is, when the marker file is written, which is after the control, the preflight and every refusal check have passed and immediately before any window loss is computed. The run refuses to start if the marker or a result file for this spec's hash already exists; the result is written once, atomically, at the end. The lock is never reopened for this spec
looks.crash: a crash after the marker that wrote no number anywhere counts as nothing seen. A re-run needs (1) the crash log saved and committed, (2) a code fix reviewed against this spec by the research-reviewer, with the spec unchanged, and (3) the fix and both attempts stated in the result; only the second run's output is published. Any number displayed or written spends the look
looks.no_peeking: before the run, the window's data are touched only by the preflight below, which prints counts and dates and no price, return, variance or loss; rehearsal of the code uses synthetic data and the spent period, never the window

control.what: before the marker, score the frozen model on the Kaggle table over 2019-01-01 to 2023-02-28 (spent data, the period vol_forecast_v1 locked) through the same loader, table builder, profile argument and scorer as the window run, and compare every cell's mean daily QLIKE for A_desk and for C_har with the committed lock scores of docs/prereg/results/vol_forecast_v1-f2d4d047ee19.json (lock.tests[cell].scores; for example NIFTY 30m C_har 0.1550)
control.tolerance: stated in advance: in each of the 8 cells, for each of A_desk and C_har, |QLIKE(control) - QLIKE(locked)| <= 0.015 (about 10% of the smallest locked value, 0.1239), and C_har's mean is below A_desk's in all 8 cells. The sources differ (Kaggle and aeron7 agree on session realised variance within 10% on 99.7% of sessions to Feb 2023), and the control lacks the sessions the review queue removes (13 and 23 Mar 2020 sit in the locked period) and the leading-gap sessions the locked run back-filled, so exact equality is not expected; a tolerance this wide is far inside the damage of a minute-of-day misalignment between the sources (the profile's first value is about 29 times its mean), which is what the control exists to catch
control.if_it_fails: the evaluation is not run and no look is spent. The cause is found and fixed in code under review (or the dataset declared unfit and a new spec written); the tolerance is not changed after seeing the control's numbers
control.scope: the control uses no window row. Its numbers are published beside the result

sessions_and_gaps.principle: no session or row is dropped, kept or reweighted because of its outcome. Every exclusion below is decided from the calendar, the importer's rules and the missing-minute mask alone, before any return, variance or loss of the window is computed, is applied identically to A_desk, B_seasonal and C_har (and to the control and the refit secondary), and is listed in full in the result with the count of rows it removed
sessions_and_gaps.grid: every session the dataset keeps for the symbol in the window, as the importer accepted it. The previous-session features, the overnight gap and the prior-5-session means of a session use the previous KEPT session of that one Kaggle table; its first sessions in the window read their lagged features from the table's own pre-March-2023 sessions (EXTERNAL_DATA item 11): features are allowed to read the past, never the label's future

expected_exclusions_by_date.importer_hard_rejects: the Muhurat evening sessions 2023-11-12, 2024-11-01 and 2025-10-21; the two 105-minute Saturdays 2024-03-02 and 2024-05-18 (fewer than 360 minutes); 2026-05-15 (truncated, already outside the window end)
expected_exclusions_by_date.importer_review_queue: three full-length weekend Budget-day sessions in the window, 2024-01-20, 2025-02-01 and 2026-02-01, are excluded by default and stay excluded: the dataset digest pins that decision, and none is reopened or taken after this registration. They are NOT outcome-neutral: the steward's note records that two of them are the window's 3rd and 10th highest-variance days for NIFTY (4th and 7th for BANKNIFTY), so the evaluation is censored at the tail, and with the hard-rejected sessions it omits about 1.8% of the window's NIFTY variance
expected_exclusions_by_date.kept_with_a_stated_feature_rule: the Mondays 2025-02-03 and 2026-02-02 stay in, and their lagged features and overnight gap come from the preceding Friday, the previous kept session
expected_exclusions_by_date.expected_other: the exchange holidays (51 of the window's 837 weekdays have no row; the run lists the weekdays without a row and states that all were checked against holiday lists, the steward's check being in EXTERNAL_DATA item 13); six kept sessions with a few missing minutes (the largest, 7 on 2023-06-14 and 6 on 2024-04-23), forward-filled by volstudy.grid. The run reports any difference between this list and what it finds

sessions_and_gaps.locked_rules_unchanged: the study's own rules apply as in vol_forecast_v1: the first 5 sessions of a series and the 5 after any break longer than 4 days have no rows (features need 5 prior consecutive sessions); a (day, decision, horizon) row whose label window has more than 20% of its minutes missing is dropped (volstudy.rows, miss_frac). The 20% rule looks at the label window, so a feed outage that coincides with a volatile stretch would be dropped; that is stated, not repaired
sessions_and_gaps.leading_gap: a session with no bar at the open is a leading-gap session: volstudy.grid back-fills its first returns from a later close, which puts the future into that session's first returns and into the next 5 sessions' priors. The build.py guard (build_tables refuses it unless allow_leading_gap) stays on, and no new exclude option is added. The run does a preflight, from the mask only, listing the leading-gap sessions of the whole Kaggle grid. If there are none, nothing changes. If there are any, the table is built with allow_leading_gap=True and, as a post-filter in the evaluation code on the table's `session` ordinal, every row of the leading-gap session and of the next 5 sessions of that symbol's grid is dropped from scoring (the control and the refit secondary too, and the refit's training rows). Under strict reuse nothing is fitted on the Kaggle data for the primary test, so there is no profile-fit exclusion. The locked run included 5 such sessions per index in its development years and never quantified their effect; this spec does not repeat that
sessions_and_gaps.unit: a session is the unit (ML_PHASE0 rule 3): the primary test is on daily losses, one per session per symbol

disclosure: Before this registration the data steward looked at the window in docs/EXTERNAL_DATA.md and recorded: the variance ranks of the three review-queue sessions inside the window (full-sample NIFTY ranks 1606, 100 and 34 of 2,789 for 2024-01-20, 2025-02-01 and 2026-02-01, and their ranks within the window), the window's share of variance removed by the hard rejections and the review queue (about 1.8% for NIFTY), session counts, and the missing-minute counts. The decision not to admit the review-queue sessions was made with that knowledge. The author of this spec saw those documents and nothing else about the window. The direction in which the omission of those days biases the difference in QLIKE between A_desk and C_har is not known; the result states that the evaluation is censored at the tail
power: Planning numbers from vol_forecast_v1's committed DEVELOPMENT folds only (2013 to 2018, six yearly out-of-sample folds per symbol and horizon); no lock-period or window number is used. The window is about 3.2 years, about 784 kept NIFTY sessions (the steward's count in EXTERNAL_DATA, itself not a model number). Against A_desk, C_har's dev QLIKE gain was 0.043 to 0.092 (16% to 35% of A's loss) and it beat A in all 48 symbol x horizon x year dev cells; the year-to-year standard deviation of the gain was 0.011 to 0.022. Treating the window mean as the mean of 3.2 independent years with that spread, the standard error is about 0.006 to 0.012, so at Holm's strictest threshold (one-sided 0.00625) and 80% power the smallest gain the test can reliably detect is about 0.020 to 0.041 QLIKE, 7% to 16% of A's loss. The dev gain is 1.6 to 2.9 times that, which puts the power at the dev gain above 99% in every cell; if the true gain in the window were half the dev gain the power would be about 98% to 99% for NIFTY and 87% for BANKNIFTY 30m, but only about 56% to 59% for BANKNIFTY 60m, 120m and close. These dev folds refit every year, whereas the primary test scores coefficients that were fixed at the end of 2018 and are 4.2 to 7.4 years old across the window, so they are optimistic about the frozen model: any decay of the coefficients lowers the true gain and the power below them (the refit secondary is there to separate that). Against B_seasonal the dev gain of C_har was 0.001 to 0.017 and the detectable gap is 0.005 to 0.030: at the dev gain the power is about 99% for NIFTY close, 71% for BANKNIFTY close and 5% to 11% in the other six cells, so the HAR layer's added value over the seasonal profile is largely undetectable cell by cell; the pooled C-versus-B test averages the cells and has more power than any one of them, but the dev numbers do not allow its power to be computed and it should not be read as confirmed power. Limits of these numbers: they use year-level spread because the daily loss differences (which the Newey-West statistic uses) are not in the committed dev numbers, so they ignore within-year autocorrelation and are a planning approximation, not the test's power; NIFTY and BANKNIFTY are strongly dependent, so 8 cells are fewer than 8 independent confirmations; the window is one realisation of the 2023 to 2026 regime (it contains no 2020-type shock, and the review queue removes three of its highest-variance days); a gain below about 7% to 16% of A's loss, an effect confined to one time of day or one calendar year, and any difference between the Kaggle source and the truth in this stretch (P0.6 addresses only what it checks) cannot be told apart by this test. A PASS is therefore strong evidence only about the large, structural advantage over A_desk that the dev folds already showed; it is weak evidence about anything finer.
controls_before_the_run: P0.6 has passed this digest and the verification record is present (run_only_after_p06); the loader refuses otherwise

record, in the run's header and the result, this spec's sha256 (autolearn.prereg.spec_hash), the code commit (clean tree), the dataset digest and status, the artifact's sha256 and the table identities (ml-build-1-<12 hex>)
rehearse the whole command on a synthetic dataset and on the spent period; a rehearsal result is discarded and never edits this spec
the preflight (counts, dates and masks only) runs before the marker; it prints no price, return, variance or loss

the window rows are read only through build.load_table(reserved_spec=<this file>), which records the spec's name in the table's attrs (the primary table with scoring_only=True, the refit secondary's table as stated in frozen_model.refit_secondary)

command.run: python -m quantdesk ml oneshot --dataset <path to ml-intake-2-feae259bdba6> --spec docs/prereg/har_oneshot_v1.json --out <an empty folder outside every git working tree>
command.needs_building: the 'oneshot' action does not exist yet: build.py's reserved window and load_table(reserved_spec=) exist, `ml build/reproduce` exist; `oneshot` is to be added to the `ml` subcommand, together with build_tables' `profile=` argument and the leading-gap post-filter, by a separate, reviewed change that implements only what this spec states and nothing else. Until it exists and is reviewed against this spec, the evaluation is not run
command.behaviour: reads every setting (window, symbols, profile_end, horizons, lags, correction, thresholds, tolerance) from the spec and takes none from the command line, so the only free arguments are the paths; there is no flag that accepts an unverified dataset. Order: refusal checks (spec sha256 not the one the reviewer recorded as merged, dataset digest other than 47d28d6376ca63af or not external_verified, artifact sha256 not the pin, a table folder inside a git working tree, a second run); the control; the preflight; the marker; the primary test, the pooled C-versus-B test and the secondaries; one atomic write. It writes nothing into docs/prereg/results itself. The result (<name>-<sha256[:12]>.json and .md, with the evidence label, the artifact's coefficients and profile, every cell, the control, the preflight lists and the secondary tables) is copied there by a person and committed, as for vol_forecast_v1
command.does_not: import the live engine, write to a journal, place or size anything, use a secret, train anything that influences a decision, or commit any third-party data

reported: the spec's sha256; dataset, digest, status and tier; the code commit; the artifact's sha256; the control; for every cell: QLIKE of each candidate, the daily-loss gain of C_har over A_desk in percent, DM t, one-sided p, Holm-adjusted p, verdict; the pooled C-versus-B test; the refit secondary (its coefficients and profile) and the other secondary tables; sessions and rows per symbol and year, kept and excluded by each rule, with the excluded sessions listed and the difference from the expected exclusions; the overall verdict (PASS, MIXED or KILL) and the opening time
use_if_passed: only as an offline research candidate for the desk's realised-volatility input, pending a separate reviewed change; its effect on option plans is judged by plan research on real point-in-time quotes, never by this study. A failure, a mixed result or a kill is final for this model and this window
